clue.text: A technological subject grasped by relative, just the same

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: to be grasped by something is to be held inside it, so the first part sits within the relative

parts.note: short for sister, a relative
IT, information technology, is a school subject

explanation.surface: A cousin or sibling has got hold of computing as a subject, and nothing has changed.
explanation.walkthrough: IT is information technology, the school subject; SIS is the usual crossword shortening of sister.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase 'as it is' means leaving matters unchanged, in their present state, so exactly the same.

indicators.note: finally points to the very end of the word before it, keeping only its closing letter

parts.note: the last letter of Hunters
to nail a criminal is to catch them

explanation.surface: Huntsmen at last capture a slow-moving animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A snail is a mollusc proverbial for its slowness, and a slug is its shell-less relative, making the description doubly apt.

clue.text: Score also announced for every player on football field?

parts.note: a score is twenty

indicators.note: what is announced is spoken out loud, so we want a word that sounds like the given one

parts.note: also means too, which is said the same as the number two

explanation.surface: A goal is noted, and something is also declared for each footballer on the pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: Score looks like a goal in a match; here it is the old word for twenty.
explanation.definitionFit: Each soccer side fields eleven players, so the whole pitch holds twenty-two men during a match; the question mark flags this numerical take.

clue.text: Prize collected by boy, absolutely correct

indicators.note: something collected by a person is taken into their hands, so one part goes inside the other

parts.note: a son is a boy
a pot is a prize, as in a trophy cup or the winnings in a game

explanation.surface: A lad picks up an award, and the verdict is that it was entirely right.
explanation.definitionFit: Spot-on is an informal British expression meaning precisely accurate or exactly right.

indicators.note: involving means including within itself, so one part wraps around the other

parts.note: a fling is a short romantic affair

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the word is taken back the other way

parts.note: a golf tee is a small peg the ball sits on

explanation.surface: A short romance with someone named Peg comes back to mind.
explanation.walkthrough: Peg looks like a woman's name; it is the small wooden support a golfer drives from.
explanation.definitionFit: Fleeting means passing swiftly and lasting only a short time, so it is a synonym of brief.

parts.note: a striker in football plays as a forward
fine as in slender, like a fine thread
a king is a ruler or leader

explanation.surface: A modern-minded attacker in football makes an excellent captain.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone forward-thinking plans ahead and favours new ideas and reform, which is what being progressive means.

indicators.note: grabbing means seizing hold of, so the jumbled letters close around another part
a drunk person is unsteady and muddled, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: letters to be rearranged
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the standard abbreviation for queen

explanation.surface: A cavalry officer, tipsy and clutching royalty, shouts the order to attack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charge!' sounds like a battle cry, but it is a verb meaning to fill with power.
explanation.definitionFit: To energise is to fill with energy or power, as you would charge a battery.

parts.note: tut is a mild exclamation of disapproval, like dear me
or is the heraldic term for gold

explanation.surface: An exclamation of surprise at a golden carriage.
explanation.walkthrough: Coach seems to be a vehicle beside gold; it is a verb meaning teach.
explanation.definitionFit: A tutor gives private teaching to a pupil, which is what a coach does.

parts.note: surface reading: something calm once every broadcasting mast has been taken away
setter's reading: the fibres that carry signals around the body have all gone, leaving one without them

explanation.surface: Things are calm once every radio transmitter has been switched off.
explanation.walkthrough: Transmitters suggests radio equipment; the setter means the body's own signal carriers, and being without them is a literal reading of a word for unflappable.
explanation.definitionFit: Being nerveless means staying calm and showing no fear, so it describes a cool, composed person.

indicators.note: something winding twists and turns, so the letters of the name are turned into a new order

parts.note: the Paris basilica's name, used as letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: The streets around the Sacré-Cœur basilica in Paris twist and turn.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for is, joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A racecourse is a track where horse races are run.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: sour or acid in taste
second meaning: a pastry case with a sweet filling

explanation.surface: A pudding with a tangy taste.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an adjective for an acidic taste and also a noun for a pastry with fruit or jam filling.

clue.text: Norse god in request for feast

indicators.note: in places the first part inside the second

parts.note: a plea is an earnest request
Thor is the Norse god of thunder

explanation.surface: A Viking deity is asked to provide a banquet.
explanation.definitionFit: A plethora is an excess or abundance, and a feast in the figurative sense is a plentiful supply.

indicators.note: heard asks for a word that sounds, when spoken, like the one indicated

parts.note: Ghana, the West African nation, said in a British accent that drops the r

explanation.surface: An instruction to acquire a nation in Africa, as told by word of mouth.
explanation.walkthrough: In standard British speech the r in the answer is silent, so it is pronounced just like Ghana.
explanation.definitionFit: To garner is to gather or collect, so it can mean to obtain.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a vast sum, as in 'cost a ...'
second meaning: in pristine, unused condition

explanation.surface: Having plenty of cash is ideal.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is informal for a huge amount of cash, and describes an item in flawless, as-new condition.

clue.text: I approach home of hawk, say, with serious intent

parts.note: taken as written
to near something is to approach it
a nest is where a bird such as a hawk lives

explanation.surface: Someone creeps up on a bird of prey's eyrie with a determined purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something in earnest means doing it sincerely and seriously rather than in jest.

indicators.note: clothes that are ill-fitting are out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: letters to be rearranged
taken as written

explanation.surface: Badly sized trousers are a total calamity.
explanation.walkthrough: Strides is British slang for trousers, which is why ill-fitting reads so naturally.
explanation.definitionFit: A disaster is a sudden event causing great damage or failure, so it is a synonym for catastrophe.

indicators.note: tidying up moves things around into a new arrangement, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A road sweeper reports having swept the road clean.
explanation.walkthrough: Cleaner looks like a person who cleans; it is a thing you wipe your mouth and fingers with.
explanation.definitionFit: A serviette is a table napkin, used at meals to wipe one's mouth and hands, so it serves as a cleaning item.

clue.text: Finished with butter, I smoked beef

parts.note: something past is over and finished
a ram butts with its head, so it is a butter
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cook done with the butter announces that they smoked some meat.
explanation.walkthrough: Butter is not the dairy spread but one who butts, a crossword favourite for a ram or goat.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastrami is highly seasoned beef brisket that is cured and then smoked.

indicators.note: a revolutionary overturns the existing order, so these letters are put in a new order

parts.note: letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A rebel has no prospect of being commemorated.
explanation.definitionFit: A cenotaph is a monument to the war dead whose bodies lie elsewhere, the best-known being in Whitehall, London.

definitions.meaning: second meaning: past tense of a verb meaning go up

explanation.surface: The price of a bottle has gone up.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosé is a pink wine, and the same letters spell the past tense of rise, meaning went up.

clue.text: Capital in those days invested in arsenic

indicators.note: money invested in something is put into it, so one part is placed inside the other

parts.note: As is the chemical symbol for arsenic
then means at that time, in those days

explanation.surface: Money from the past was sunk into a poison business.
explanation.walkthrough: Capital seems to be money, given invested; it is a nation's chief city.
explanation.definitionFit: Greece's seat of government is this ancient city, an example of a capital, so it is a definition by example.

clue.text: Just behind front of fire alarm

indicators.note: behind says the first part follows after the second in the answer
the front of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: the first letter of fire
just and right both mean fair or proper

explanation.surface: Someone standing close to the blaze sets off a warning bell.
explanation.walkthrough: Just looks like 'only' or 'barely'; here it means fair.
explanation.definitionFit: Fright is a sudden feeling of fear, and alarm can mean exactly that sudden fear.

clue.text: Someone on the way out: in leaving, one rueful

indicators.note: in tells us the answer lies inside the words that follow, running across them

parts.note: letters running across the end of leaving, all of one and the start of rueful

explanation.surface: A person departing feels a pang of regret on going.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface invites charade pieces such as GONE for leaving; the letters are simply sitting in a row: leavinG ONE Rueful.
explanation.definitionFit: This informal noun means a person who is doomed or close to death, beyond any hope of rescue.

clue.text: Extraordinary state in Texas originally most stylish

indicators.note: extraordinary means out of the ordinary, so the letters are taken out of their usual order

parts.note: letters to be rearranged

indicators.note: originally points to how a word begins, so only its opening letter is used

parts.note: the first letter of Texas

explanation.surface: An unusual US state boasts the sharpest dressers in Texas.
explanation.definitionFit: Natty is an informal British word for smart and dapper, so the superlative means the smartest dressed.

indicators.note: in places the selected letter inside the next part

parts.note: to bar is to stop or prevent

indicators.note: initially signals the opening letter of the word just before it

parts.note: the first letter of raging

explanation.surface: A furious outburst starts up in a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A strop is a fit of bad temper or sulking, in informal British English.

indicators.note: some means only part of the following words, so the answer is a run of letters inside them

parts.note: letters running across the end of scoter and the start of naturally

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher notes that a scoter, a kind of sea duck, is of course a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: Hidden in scoTER Naturally; a scoter is a dark sea duck, a nicely chosen camouflage.
explanation.definitionFit: A tern is a slender seabird with forked tail, related to gulls.

clue.text: Fruit in an ornate tray, nourishing

indicators.note: in places the first part inside what follows
ornate means elaborately worked, so the following word is reworked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
a lime is a citrus fruit
letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A citrus fruit sits on a decorated serving tray, offering sustenance.
explanation.walkthrough: The fruit sits inside AN, and the rearranged tray follows on after.
explanation.definitionFit: Alimentary means relating to food and nourishment, as in the alimentary canal that digests it.

clue.text: Marvellous Scottish city, did you say?

indicators.note: did you say asks us to go by the spoken sound rather than the spelling

parts.note: Stirling is a historic city in central Scotland

explanation.surface: Someone praises a wonderful town in Scotland and asks for confirmation.
explanation.definitionFit: Sterling as an adjective means excellent or of great worth, as in sterling work, so it matches wonderful.

clue.text: One of seven characters dropping off?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: one of Snow White's seven dwarfs in the Disney film
second meaning: drowsy, nodding off to sleep

explanation.walkthrough: Seven characters suggests a seven-letter word or text; it means the Disney dwarfs.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleepy is the name of a dwarf in Disney's Snow White, and the adjective describes someone drowsy and about to doze.
